passage:
Lisa dropped her phone, and the screen cracked. She was upset because she used it for messages, homework photos, and music.
Her mother said she would help pay for the repair, but Lisa had to pay part of it herself.
For three weeks, Lisa saved money. She stopped buying drinks after school and brought water from home. She also helped her aunt clean the shop on weekends.
When the phone was repaired, Lisa used it more carefully. She bought a stronger case with her own money.
The crack disappeared from the screen, but the lesson stayed. Things often feel more valuable when people understand what it costs to fix them.
